282	class WOTSOneTimeSigner:
283	    """Thread-safe, single-use wrapper around a :class:`WOTSPrivateKey`.
284	
285	    The first :meth:`sign` call returns the ordinary :func:`wots_sign`
286	    signature and marks the key as used; every later call raises
287	    :class:`~pqattest.KeyExhaustedError`. The guard is per instance and per
288	    process — copying the private key, calling the stateless :func:`wots_sign`
289	    directly or reusing the key in another process is the caller's
290	    responsibility. State can be persisted with :meth:`checkpoint` and
291	    restored in another process with :meth:`from_checkpoint`; the checkpoint
292	    contains the private key in the clear and is protected only by a SHA-256
293	    checksum against accidental corruption, so callers must store it securely.
294	    :meth:`sign_with_checkpoint` pairs the single signature with the
295	    post-sign checkpoint in one atomic call.
296	    """
297	
298	    __slots__ = ("_lock", "_private_key", "_public_key", "_used")
299	
300	    def __init__(self, private_key: WOTSPrivateKey) -> None:
301	        if not isinstance(private_key, WOTSPrivateKey):
302	            raise TypeError("private_key must be a WOTSPrivateKey")
303	        self._restore_state(private_key, self._public_key_from(private_key), False)
304	
305	    @staticmethod
306	    def _public_key_from(private_key: WOTSPrivateKey) -> WOTSPublicKey:
307	        b = 1 << private_key.w
308	        return WOTSPublicKey(
309	            w=private_key.w,
310	            elements=tuple(
311	                _chain_walk(start, b - 1) for start in private_key.elements
312	            ),
313	        )
314	
315	    def _restore_state(
316	        self,
317	        private_key: WOTSPrivateKey,
318	        public_key: WOTSPublicKey,
319	        used: bool,
320	    ) -> None:
321	        self._lock = threading.Lock()
322	        self._private_key = private_key
323	        self._public_key = public_key
324	        self._used = used
325	
326	    @property
327	    def public_key(self) -> WOTSPublicKey:
328	        """Public key derived from the wrapped private key (read-only)."""
329	        return self._public_key
330	
331	    @property
332	    def used(self) -> bool:
333	        """``True`` once a signature has been produced (read-only)."""
334	        return self._used
335	
336	    def sign(self, message: Any) -> tuple[bytes, ...]:
337	        """Sign once.
338	
339	        Behaves exactly like :func:`wots_sign` on the first successful call,
340	        accepting ``bytes``/``bytearray``/``str``; an unsupported message type
341	        raises the same ``TypeError`` that :func:`wots_sign` raises without
342	        consuming the key. Any later call raises
343	        :class:`~pqattest.KeyExhaustedError`. Concurrent calls are serialised
344	        on one lock so that at most one succeeds and every loser raises
345	        :class:`~pqattest.KeyExhaustedError`.
346	        """
347	        with self._lock:
348	            if self._used:
349	                raise KeyExhaustedError("this one-time signing key has already been used")
350	            signature = wots_sign(message, self._private_key)
351	            self._used = True
352	            return signature
353	
354	    def _checkpoint_bytes(self) -> bytes:
355	        """Serialise the signer state; the caller holds the lock."""
356	        body = (
357	            _CHECKPOINT_MAGIC
358	            + bytes((_CHECKPOINT_VERSION, self._private_key.w, int(self._used)))
359	            + len(self._private_key.elements).to_bytes(2, "big")
360	            + b"".join(self._private_key.elements)
361	        )
362	        return body + hashlib.sha256(body).digest()
363	
364	    def checkpoint(self) -> bytes:
365	        """Serialise the signer state (private key plus ``used``) to ``bytes``.
366	
367	        The v1 layout is: the 8-byte magic ``b"PQAWCP\\0\\0"``; one byte each
368	        for the version (1), ``w`` and ``used`` (0 or 1); the element count as
369	        2 big-endian bytes (67 for ``w=4``, 34 for ``w=8``); every private key
370	        element in chain order (32 bytes each); and finally the SHA-256 of all
371	        preceding content. Encoding is deterministic: the same state always
372	        produces the same bytes.
373	
374	        The checkpoint shares the signing lock, so a concurrent snapshot
375	        reflects the state either immediately before or immediately after an
376	        in-flight :meth:`sign`, never part-way through one. The blob contains
377	        the private key in the clear and the trailing hash only detects
378	        accidental corruption — store it as a secret.
379	        """
380	        with self._lock:
381	            return self._checkpoint_bytes()
382	
383	    def sign_with_checkpoint(self, message: Any) -> tuple[tuple[bytes, ...], bytes]:
384	        """Sign once and snapshot the used state in one atomic step.
385	
386	        Behaves like :meth:`sign` — same ``bytes``/``bytearray``/``str``
387	        message rules, same one-time W-OTS signature and the same
388	        post-sign ``used=True`` state, all under the signing lock — but
389	        instead of the signature alone it returns ``(signature,
390	        checkpoint)``: the first half is the ordinary immutable signature
391	        tuple that :meth:`sign` returns, value-for-value identical to
392	        calling :meth:`sign` on the same message from the same starting
393	        state, and the second is the ``bytes`` that :meth:`checkpoint`
394	        returns immediately after signing, byte-for-byte the same v1
395	        encoding holding the private key and ``used=1``. Pairing the two
396	        halves in one call keeps the signature and the state it advanced
397	        to together, so a caller can never match a signature against a
398	        checkpoint taken at the wrong point under concurrency.
399	
400	        A rejected message type raises ``TypeError`` without consuming the
401	        key, and an already used instance raises
402	        :class:`~pqattest.KeyExhaustedError`; a failed call returns no
403	        partial result. The whole call — signature, ``used`` flip and
404	        snapshot — linearises with :meth:`sign` and :meth:`checkpoint`
405	        under the same lock, so at most one concurrent caller succeeds,
406	        and no randomness is drawn. The returned checkpoint still carries
407	        the private key in the clear and its trailing hash only detects
408	        accidental corruption — it offers no authentication, encryption or
409	        atomic persistence, so confidentiality, durable storage and
410	        rollback protection remain the caller's responsibility.
411	        """
412	        message = _as_bytes(message)
413	        with self._lock:
414	            if self._used:
415	                raise KeyExhaustedError("this one-time signing key has already been used")
416	            signature = wots_sign(message, self._private_key)
417	            self._used = True
418	            return signature, self._checkpoint_bytes()
419	
420	    def sign_with_auth_state(
421	        self, message: Any, *, key: Any, generation: Any
422	    ) -> tuple[tuple[bytes, ...], bytes]:
423	        """Sign once and return the advanced state as a v2 auth envelope.
424	
425	        Behaves like :meth:`sign` — same ``bytes``/``bytearray``/``str``
426	        message rules, same one-time signature and the same post-sign
427	        ``used=True`` state, all under the signing lock — but instead of the
428	        signature alone it returns ``(signature, envelope)``: the first half
429	        is the ordinary immutable W-OTS signature tuple that :meth:`sign`
430	        returns, and the second is the :func:`auth_state_wrap` v2 envelope
431	        (``bytes``) over the v1 :meth:`checkpoint` bytes of the used state
432	        with ``scheme="wots"`` and the given ``key`` and ``generation``. The
433	        wrapped checkpoint is byte-for-byte identical to the one
434	        :meth:`checkpoint` returns immediately after signing, so the envelope
435	        is byte-for-byte identical to signing and then wrapping an explicit
436	        checkpoint. Pairing the two halves in one call keeps the signature
437	        and the state it advanced to together, so a caller can never match a
438	        signature against a checkpoint taken at the wrong point under
439	        concurrency.
440	
441	        Every argument is validated before the key is spent: ``key`` is
442	        keyword-only and must be a non-empty ``bytes``/``bytearray`` shared
443	        secret; ``generation`` is keyword-only and must be a non-boolean
444	        integer in ``0 .. 2**64 - 1``. A wrong message or key type raises
445	        ``TypeError``; an empty key or an out-of-range generation raises
446	        ``ValueError``; an already used instance raises
447	        :class:`~pqattest.KeyExhaustedError`. Every failure leaves ``used``
448	        untouched and returns no partial result. The whole call — signature,
449	        ``used`` flip, snapshot and wrapping — linearises with :meth:`sign`
450	        and :meth:`checkpoint` under the same lock, and no randomness is
451	        drawn. The envelope is plaintext and authenticated only; it provides
452	        neither encryption nor protection against replay or rollback on its
453	        own.
454	        """
455	        message = _as_bytes(message)
456	        key_bytes = _validate_key(key)
457	        generation_value = _validate_generation(generation, "generation")
458	        with self._lock:
459	            if self._used:
460	                raise KeyExhaustedError("this one-time signing key has already been used")
461	            signature = wots_sign(message, self._private_key)
462	            self._used = True
463	            checkpoint = self._checkpoint_bytes()
464	            envelope = auth_state_wrap(
465	                checkpoint,
466	                scheme="wots",
467	                key=key_bytes,
468	                generation=generation_value,
469	            )
470	            return signature, envelope
471	
472	    @classmethod
473	    def from_checkpoint(cls, data: Any) -> "WOTSOneTimeSigner":
474	        """Restore a signer from ``checkpoint()`` output without randomness.
475	
476	        ``data`` must be ``bytes`` or ``bytearray``; anything else raises
477	        ``TypeError``. A bad magic, version, ``w``, ``used`` flag, element
478	        count, length, truncation, trailing data or checksum mismatch raises
479	        ``ValueError`` and no instance is returned. The private key and the
480	        public key rebuilt from it are identical to the original's, so a
481	        restored unused signer still allows exactly one signature and a
482	        checkpoint taken after signing restores a signer whose every call
483	        raises :class:`~pqattest.KeyExhaustedError`.
484	        """
485	        if not isinstance(data, (bytes, bytearray)):
486	            raise TypeError("checkpoint data must be bytes or bytearray")
487	        data = bytes(data)
488	        header = _CHECKPOINT_HEADER_BYTES
489	        if len(data) < header + _CHECKPOINT_CHECKSUM_BYTES:
490	            raise ValueError("checkpoint is too short")
491	        body, checksum = data[:-_CHECKPOINT_CHECKSUM_BYTES], data[-_CHECKPOINT_CHECKSUM_BYTES:]
492	        if body[:8] != _CHECKPOINT_MAGIC:
493	            raise ValueError("bad checkpoint magic")
494	        if body[8] != _CHECKPOINT_VERSION:
495	            raise ValueError(f"unsupported checkpoint version: {body[8]}")
496	        w = _validate_w(body[9])
497	        used_byte = body[10]
498	        if used_byte not in (0, 1):
499	            raise ValueError("used flag must be 0 or 1")
500	        element_count = int.from_bytes(body[11:13], "big")
501	        _, l1, l2 = _params(w)
502	        chains = l1 + l2
503	        if element_count != chains:
504	            raise ValueError("element count does not match the chain count for w")
505	        if len(body) != header + element_count * ELEMENT_BYTES:
506	            raise ValueError("checkpoint length does not match the element count")
507	        if hashlib.sha256(body).digest() != checksum:
508	            raise ValueError("checkpoint checksum mismatch")
509	        elements = tuple(
510	            body[header + i * ELEMENT_BYTES : header + (i + 1) * ELEMENT_BYTES]
511	            for i in range(element_count)
512	        )
513	        private_key = WOTSPrivateKey(w=w, elements=elements)
514	        signer = cls.__new__(cls)
515	        signer._restore_state(
516	            private_key, cls._public_key_from(private_key), bool(used_byte)
517	        )
518	        return signer
519	
520	    @classmethod
521	    def from_auth_state(
522	        cls, data: Any, *, key: Any, min_generation: Any = None, claim: Any
523	    ) -> tuple["WOTSOneTimeSigner", int]:
524	        """Restore a signer from a v2 ``"wots"`` envelope and claim it once.
525	
526	        Combines v2 verification, the generation floor and the v1 checkpoint
527	        restore in one call without drawing randomness, and — only once
528	        everything has succeeded — performs the external monotonic claim so a
529	        caller can never accept a restored key without also claiming its
530	        generation. Only an envelope produced by :func:`auth_state_wrap` with
531	        ``scheme="wots"`` is accepted; no new format is introduced.
532	        ``key``, ``min_generation`` and ``claim`` are keyword-only. Returns
533	        ``(signer, generation)``: the restored :class:`WOTSOneTimeSigner`
534	        (equal to :meth:`from_checkpoint` on the embedded payload) and the
535	        non-negative uint64 generation carried in the envelope.
536	
537	        ``data`` must be ``bytes`` or ``bytearray``; ``key`` must be a
538	        non-empty ``bytes``/``bytearray`` shared secret; ``min_generation``
539	        must be ``None`` or a non-boolean integer in ``0 .. 2**64 - 1``;
540	        ``claim`` must be callable. A wrong type (including a boolean floor or
541	        a non-callable claim) raises ``TypeError``. The v2 HMAC tag is
542	        verified first with :func:`hmac.compare_digest`; the envelope scheme
543	        is then fixed to ``"wots"``, the payload magic checked and the
544	        generation floor applied; only afterwards is the untouched payload
545	        handed to :meth:`from_checkpoint`. Once the checkpoint is restored,
546	        ``claim`` is called exactly once with the single token
547	        ``("wots", generation)``; the restore succeeds only when that call
548	        returns ``True`` (compared by identity), and any exception it raises
549	        propagates untouched. An empty key, a bad tag or envelope, a non-wots
550	        scheme (including a v1 envelope), a generation below the floor, an
551	        invalid checkpoint, or a claim that is not ``True`` raises
552	        ``ValueError`` and the callback is never invoked on such a failure.
553	        """
554	        return _restore_auth_state(
555	            "wots",
556	            data,
557	            key=key,
558	            min_generation=min_generation,
559	            claim=claim,
560	            restore=cls.from_checkpoint,
561	        )
562

564	def wots_keygen(
565	    *,
566	    w: int = 4,
567	    token_bytes: Callable[[int], bytes] = secrets.token_bytes,
568	) -> tuple[WOTSPrivateKey, WOTSPublicKey]:
569	    """Generate a fresh W-OTS key pair.
570	
571	    ``w`` selects the Winternitz parameter and must be 4 or 8. Every chain
572	    starts at a random 32-byte value from ``token_bytes``; the public key
573	    stores each chain's step ``B - 1`` endpoint.
574	    """
575	    w = _validate_w(w)
576	    b, l1, l2 = _params(w)
577	    starts = tuple(bytes(token_bytes(ELEMENT_BYTES)) for _ in range(l1 + l2))
578	    for start in starts:
579	        if len(start) != ELEMENT_BYTES:
580	            raise ValueError(f"token_bytes must return {ELEMENT_BYTES} bytes")
581	    private_key = WOTSPrivateKey(w=w, elements=starts)
582	    endpoints = tuple(_chain_walk(start, b - 1) for start in starts)
583	    return private_key, WOTSPublicKey(w=w, elements=endpoints)
584	
585	
586	def wots_sign(message: Any, private_key: WOTSPrivateKey) -> tuple[bytes, ...]:
587	    """Sign ``message``: for each digit ``d`` reveal chain value at step ``d``.
588	
589	    Message digits come first, followed by the fixed-width checksum digits.
590	    """
591	    if not isinstance(private_key, WOTSPrivateKey):
592	        raise TypeError("private_key must be a WOTSPrivateKey")
593	    digits = _signing_digits(message, private_key.w)
594	    return tuple(
595	        _chain_walk(private_key.elements[i], digit)
596	        for i, digit in enumerate(digits)
597	    )
598	
599	
600	def wots_verify(
601	    message: Any, signature: Sequence[Any], public_key: WOTSPublicKey
602	) -> bool:
603	    """Complete the remaining chain steps and compare every public endpoint.
604	
605	    Returns ``False`` for any structural, parameter or content mismatch; only
606	    a wrong key *type* raises ``TypeError``.
607	    """
608	    if not isinstance(public_key, WOTSPublicKey):
609	        raise TypeError("public_key must be a WOTSPublicKey")
610	    w = public_key.w
611	    b, l1, l2 = _params(w)
612	    length = l1 + l2
613	
614	    try:
615	        parts = tuple(bytes(part) for part in signature)
616	    except (TypeError, ValueError):
617	        return False
618	    if len(parts) != length or len(public_key.elements) != length:
619	        return False
620	    if any(len(part) != ELEMENT_BYTES for part in parts):
621	        return False
622	
623	    try:
624	        digits = _signing_digits(message, w)
625	    except TypeError:
626	        return False
627	    for i, digit in enumerate(digits):
628	        endpoint = _chain_walk(parts[i], b - 1 - digit)
629	        if endpoint != public_key.elements[i]:
630	            return False
631	    return True
632

634	def wots_signature_to_bytes(signature: Any, *, w: int) -> bytes:
635	    """Serialise a stateless W-OTS signature to the versioned v1 wire format.
636	
637	    ``signature`` must be a ``tuple`` whose members are all ``bytes`` — the
638	    shape :func:`wots_sign` returns; anything else raises ``TypeError``.
639	    ``w`` is keyword-only and must be 4 or 8 (``ValueError`` otherwise); the
640	    signature must contain exactly the chain count for ``w`` (67 or 34
641	    elements) and every element must be exactly 32 bytes, else ``ValueError``.
642	
643	    The layout is the 8-byte magic ``b"PQAWSIG\\0"``; one byte each for the
644	    version (1) and ``w``; the element count as 2 big-endian bytes; then every
645	    signature element in chain order, 32 bytes each. Encoding is
646	    deterministic: the same signature and ``w`` always produce the same
647	    bytes.
648	    """
649	    if not isinstance(signature, tuple):
650	        raise TypeError("signature must be a tuple of 32-byte values")
651	    for element in signature:
652	        if not isinstance(element, bytes):
653	            raise TypeError("every signature element must be bytes")
654	    w = _validate_w(w)
655	    chains = _chain_count(w)
656	    if len(signature) != chains:
657	        raise ValueError(f"signature must contain exactly {chains} elements for w={w}")
658	    for element in signature:
659	        if len(element) != ELEMENT_BYTES:
660	            raise ValueError(f"every signature element must be exactly {ELEMENT_BYTES} bytes")
661	    return _encode_v1(_SIGNATURE_MAGIC, w, signature)
662	
663	
664	def wots_signature_from_bytes(data: Any) -> tuple[int, tuple[bytes, ...]]:
665	    """Parse ``wots_signature_to_bytes()`` output back into ``(w, elements)``.
666	
667	    ``data`` must be ``bytes`` or ``bytearray``; anything else raises
668	    ``TypeError``. A bad magic, an unknown version, an invalid ``w``, an
669	    element count that does not match the chain count for ``w``, truncation
670	    or trailing data raises ``ValueError``. The returned ``elements`` are an
671	    immutable ``tuple`` of 32-byte ``bytes`` in the original chain order,
672	    ready for :func:`wots_verify`.
673	    """
674	    return _decode_v1(data, _SIGNATURE_MAGIC, "signature")
675	
676	
677	def _wots_signature_matches_key(signature: Any, public_key: Any) -> bool:
678	    """Non-raising parameter/count check for a W-OTS proof pair."""
679	    if not isinstance(public_key, WOTSPublicKey):
680	        return False
681	    try:
682	        w = _validate_w(public_key.w)
683	    except (ValueError, AttributeError):
684	        return False
685	    if not isinstance(signature, tuple) or len(signature) != _chain_count(w):
686	        return False
687	    return all(
688	        isinstance(element, bytes) and len(element) == ELEMENT_BYTES
689	        for element in signature
690	    )
691	
692	
693	@dataclass(frozen=True)
694	class WOTSProof:
695	    """Frozen, self-contained bundle of one W-OTS public key and one signature.
696	
697	    Unlike a bare signature tuple (whose wire encoding needs ``w`` supplied
698	    separately), a proof carries the :class:`WOTSPublicKey` that constrains
699	    its signature, so it can be transported on its own as a single byte block
700	    and verified with :meth:`verify`. The proof stores no message and is a
701	    pure serialisation container: it offers neither authentication nor
702	    encryption of the wrapper itself, draws no randomness, generates
703	    no keys and keeps no state.
704	    """
705	
706	    public_key: WOTSPublicKey
707	    signature: tuple[bytes, ...]
708	
709	    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
710	        if not isinstance(self.public_key, WOTSPublicKey):
711	            raise TypeError("public_key must be a WOTSPublicKey")
712	        if not isinstance(self.signature, tuple):
713	            raise TypeError("signature must be a tuple of 32-byte values")
714	        if not all(isinstance(element, bytes) for element in self.signature):
715	            raise TypeError("every signature element must be bytes")
716	        if not _wots_signature_matches_key(self.signature, self.public_key):
717	            raise ValueError(
718	                "signature chain count or elements do not match the public key"
719	            )
720	
721	    def to_bytes(self) -> bytes:
722	        """Serialise to the versioned v1 proof wire format as ``bytes``.
723	
724	        The layout is the 8-byte magic ``b"PQAWPRF\\0"``; one version byte
725	        (1); the public-key and signature lengths as 4 big-endian bytes each;
726	        then the existing v1 encodings of the public key and of the signature
727	        constrained by that key, in that order (the inner encodings are
728	        reused unchanged). Encoding is deterministic: the same proof always
729	        produces the same bytes. A field corrupted by bypassing the frozen
730	        constructor raises ``ValueError`` instead of producing malformed
731	        bytes.
732	        """
733	        if not isinstance(self, WOTSProof):
734	            raise TypeError("to_bytes must be called on a WOTSProof")
735	        try:
736	            key_bytes = self.public_key.to_bytes()
737	            signature_bytes = wots_signature_to_bytes(
738	                self.signature, w=self.public_key.w
739	            )
740	        except (TypeError, AttributeError) as exc:
741	            raise ValueError(f"corrupted proof field: {exc}") from exc
742	        return (
743	            _PROOF_MAGIC
744	            + bytes((_PROOF_VERSION,))
745	            + len(key_bytes).to_bytes(4, "big")
746	            + len(signature_bytes).to_bytes(4, "big")
747	            + key_bytes
748	            + signature_bytes
749	        )
750	
751	    @classmethod
752	    def from_bytes(cls, data: Any) -> "WOTSProof":
753	        """Parse ``to_bytes()`` output back into a :class:`WOTSProof`.
754	
755	        ``data`` must be ``bytes`` or ``bytearray``; anything else raises
756	        ``TypeError``. The embedded public key is recovered first and then
757	        constrains the signature. A bad magic, an unknown version, a length
758	        field that is out of bounds or disagrees with the actual content,
759	        truncation, trailing data, an invalid nested encoding, or a signature
760	        inconsistent with the key (wrong ``w`` or chain count) raises
761	        ``ValueError`` and no half-valid object is returned.
762	        """
763	        if not isinstance(data, (bytes, bytearray)):
764	            raise TypeError("proof data must be bytes or bytearray")
765	        data = bytes(data)
766	        if len(data) < _PROOF_HEADER_BYTES:
767	            raise ValueError("proof encoding is truncated")
768	        if data[:8] != _PROOF_MAGIC:
769	            raise ValueError("bad proof magic")
770	        if data[8] != _PROOF_VERSION:
771	            raise ValueError(f"unsupported proof version: {data[8]}")
772	        key_length = int.from_bytes(data[9:13], "big")
773	        signature_length = int.from_bytes(data[13:17], "big")
774	        key_end = _PROOF_HEADER_BYTES + key_length
775	        signature_end = key_end + signature_length
776	        if key_length == 0 or signature_length == 0:
777	            raise ValueError("a length field must not be zero")
778	        if key_end > len(data) or signature_end > len(data):
779	            raise ValueError("proof encoding is truncated")
780	        if signature_end < len(data):
781	            raise ValueError("trailing data after the proof encoding")
782	        public_key = WOTSPublicKey.from_bytes(data[_PROOF_HEADER_BYTES:key_end])
783	        w, signature = wots_signature_from_bytes(data[key_end:signature_end])
784	        if w != public_key.w:
785	            raise ValueError("signature w does not match the public key")
786	        return cls(public_key=public_key, signature=signature)
787	
788	    def verify(self, message: Any) -> bool:
789	        """Verify the embedded signature against the embedded public key.
790	
791	        Accepts ``bytes``/``bytearray``/``str`` exactly like
792	        :func:`wots_verify`, to which this call delegates; it returns
793	        ``True`` only for the message that was actually signed. Any change to
794	        the message, public key or signature, an illegal message type, or
795	        fields corrupted by bypassing the frozen constructor returns
796	        ``False`` instead of raising. The proof itself carries no message and
797	        cannot authenticate its own origin.
798	        """
799	        try:
800	            return wots_verify(message, self.signature, self.public_key)
801	        except Exception:
802	            return False

"""Winternitz one-time signature (W-OTS) for pqattest.

Like the Lamport construction this is a **one-time** signature: a key pair
must sign at most one message. Each signing key is a set of hash chains; a
signature for a base-``B`` digit ``d`` reveals the value at chain step ``d``
and the public key holds the step ``B - 1`` endpoint. Only the standard
library is used. Keys and signatures have a deterministic, versioned v1
binary codec: :meth:`WOTSPrivateKey.to_bytes` /
:meth:`WOTSPrivateKey.from_bytes`, :meth:`WOTSPublicKey.to_bytes` /
:meth:`WOTSPublicKey.from_bytes`, and the stateless
:func:`wots_signature_to_bytes` / :func:`wots_signature_from_bytes`. The
private-key encoding contains the secret in the clear, so callers must store
it securely. :class:`WOTSOneTimeSigner` state can be persisted with a
versioned binary checkpoint (``checkpoint`` / ``from_checkpoint``); the blob
holds the private key in the clear and is integrity-protected only by a
SHA-256 checksum, so callers must store it securely.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import secrets
import threading
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any, Callable, Iterable, Sequence

from ._errors import KeyExhaustedError
from .auth import (
    _restore_auth_state,
    _validate_generation,
    _validate_key,
    auth_state_wrap,
)

__all__ = [
    "ELEMENT_BYTES",
    "WOTSOneTimeSigner",
    "WOTSPrivateKey",
    "WOTSProof",
    "WOTSPublicKey",
    "wots_keygen",
    "wots_sign",
    "wots_signature_from_bytes",
    "wots_signature_to_bytes",
    "wots_verify",
]

ELEMENT_BYTES = 32
_DOMAIN = b"pqattest/wots/v1"
_ALLOWED_W = (4, 8)

_CHECKPOINT_MAGIC = b"PQAWCP\0\0"
_CHECKPOINT_VERSION = 1
_CHECKPOINT_HEADER_BYTES = 8 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 2
_CHECKPOINT_CHECKSUM_BYTES = 32

_PRIVATE_KEY_MAGIC = b"PQAWPRV\0"
_PUBLIC_KEY_MAGIC = b"PQAWPUB\0"
_SIGNATURE_MAGIC = b"PQAWSIG\0"
_CODEC_VERSION = 1
_CODEC_HEADER_BYTES = 8 + 1 + 1 + 2

_PROOF_MAGIC = b"PQAWPRF\0"
_PROOF_VERSION = 1
_PROOF_HEADER_BYTES = 8 + 1 + 4 + 4


def _as_bytes(message: Any) -> bytes:
    if isinstance(message, bytes):
        return message
    if isinstance(message, bytearray):
        return bytes(message)
    if isinstance(message, str):
        return message.encode("utf-8")
    raise TypeError("message must be bytes, bytearray or str")


def _validate_w(w: Any) -> int:
    if isinstance(w, bool) or not isinstance(w, int) or w not in _ALLOWED_W:
        raise ValueError("w must be 4 or 8")
    return w


def _params(w: int) -> tuple[int, int, int]:
    """Return ``(B, l1, l2)``: base, message digit count, checksum digit count."""
    b = 1 << w
    l1 = 256 // w
    l2 = 1
    limit = l1 * (b - 1)
    while b ** l2 <= limit:
        l2 += 1
    return b, l1, l2


def _validate_elements(w: int, elements: Any) -> None:
    if not isinstance(elements, tuple):
        raise TypeError("elements must be a tuple of 32-byte values")
    _, l1, l2 = _params(w)
    if len(elements) != l1 + l2:
        raise ValueError(f"elements must contain exactly {l1 + l2} values for w={w}")
    for element in elements:
        if not isinstance(element, bytes) or len(element) != ELEMENT_BYTES:
            raise ValueError(f"every element must be exactly {ELEMENT_BYTES} bytes")


def _chain_count(w: int) -> int:
    _, l1, l2 = _params(w)
    return l1 + l2


def _encode_v1(magic: bytes, w: int, elements: tuple[bytes, ...]) -> bytes:
    """Shared v1 layout: magic, version, ``w``, element count, elements."""
    return (
        magic
        + bytes((_CODEC_VERSION, w))
        + len(elements).to_bytes(2, "big")
        + b"".join(elements)
    )


def _decode_v1(data: Any, magic: bytes, name: str) -> tuple[int, tuple[bytes, ...]]:
    """Parse a v1 blob into ``(w, elements)``; ``name`` labels error messages."""
    if not isinstance(data, (bytes, bytearray)):
        raise TypeError(f"{name} data must be bytes or bytearray")
    data = bytes(data)
    if len(data) < _CODEC_HEADER_BYTES:
        raise ValueError(f"{name} encoding is truncated")
    if data[:8] != magic:
        raise ValueError(f"bad {name} magic")
    if data[8] != _CODEC_VERSION:
        raise ValueError(f"unsupported {name} version: {data[8]}")
    w = _validate_w(data[9])
    element_count = int.from_bytes(data[10:12], "big")
    chains = _chain_count(w)
    if element_count != chains:
        raise ValueError("element count does not match the chain count for w")
    expected = _CODEC_HEADER_BYTES + element_count * ELEMENT_BYTES
    if len(data) < expected:
        raise ValueError(f"{name} encoding is truncated")
    if len(data) > expected:
        raise ValueError(f"trailing data after the {name} encoding")
    elements = tuple(
        data[_CODEC_HEADER_BYTES + i * ELEMENT_BYTES : _CODEC_HEADER_BYTES + (i + 1) * ELEMENT_BYTES]
        for i in range(element_count)
    )
    return w, elements


def _key_to_bytes(key: Any, key_type: type, magic: bytes, name: str) -> bytes:
    if not isinstance(key, key_type):
        raise TypeError(f"to_bytes must be called on a {key_type.__name__}")
    try:
        w = _validate_w(key.w)
        _validate_elements(w, key.elements)
    except TypeError as exc:
        raise ValueError(f"corrupted {name}: {exc}") from exc
    return _encode_v1(magic, w, key.elements)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class WOTSPrivateKey:
    """Frozen W-OTS private key.

    ``elements`` holds the random step-0 start value of every chain: the
    ``l1`` message chains followed by the ``l2`` checksum chains.
    """

    w: int
    elements: tuple[bytes, ...]

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        w = _validate_w(self.w)
        _validate_elements(w, self.elements)

    @property
    def length(self) -> int:
        """Number of chains (and signature elements): ``l1 + l2``."""
        return len(self.elements)

    def to_bytes(self) -> bytes:
        """Serialise to the versioned v1 wire format as ``bytes``.

        The layout is the 8-byte magic ``b"PQAWPRV\\0"``; one byte each for
        the version (1) and ``w``; the element count as 2 big-endian bytes
        (67 for ``w=4``, 34 for ``w=8``); then every private element in chain
        order, 32 bytes each. Encoding is deterministic: the same key always
        produces the same bytes. Fields corrupted by bypassing the frozen
        constructor raise ``ValueError`` instead of producing a malformed
        encoding. The blob contains the private key in the clear — store it
        as a secret.
        """
        return _key_to_bytes(self, WOTSPrivateKey, _PRIVATE_KEY_MAGIC, "private key")

    @classmethod
    def from_bytes(cls, data: Any) -> "WOTSPrivateKey":
        """Parse ``to_bytes()`` output back into a :class:`WOTSPrivateKey`.

        ``data`` must be ``bytes`` or ``bytearray``; anything else raises
        ``TypeError``. A bad magic, an unknown version, an invalid ``w``, an
        element count that does not match the chain count for ``w``,
        truncation or trailing data raises ``ValueError`` and no instance is
        returned. The restored key is equal by value to the original.
        """
        w, elements = _decode_v1(data, _PRIVATE_KEY_MAGIC, "private key")
        return cls(w=w, elements=elements)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class WOTSPublicKey:
    """Frozen W-OTS public key: the step ``B - 1`` endpoint of every chain."""

    w: int
    elements: tuple[bytes, ...]

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        w = _validate_w(self.w)
        _validate_elements(w, self.elements)

    @property
    def length(self) -> int:
        """Number of chains (and signature elements): ``l1 + l2``."""
        return len(self.elements)

    def to_bytes(self) -> bytes:
        """Serialise to the versioned v1 wire format as ``bytes``.

        The layout is the 8-byte magic ``b"PQAWPUB\\0"``; one byte each for
        the version (1) and ``w``; the element count as 2 big-endian bytes
        (67 for ``w=4``, 34 for ``w=8``); then every public element in chain
        order, 32 bytes each. Encoding is deterministic: the same key always
        produces the same bytes. Fields corrupted by bypassing the frozen
        constructor raise ``ValueError`` instead of producing a malformed
        encoding.
        """
        return _key_to_bytes(self, WOTSPublicKey, _PUBLIC_KEY_MAGIC, "public key")

    @classmethod
    def from_bytes(cls, data: Any) -> "WOTSPublicKey":
        """Parse ``to_bytes()`` output back into a :class:`WOTSPublicKey`.

        ``data`` must be ``bytes`` or ``bytearray``; anything else raises
        ``TypeError``. A bad magic, an unknown version, an invalid ``w``, an
        element count that does not match the chain count for ``w``,
        truncation or trailing data raises ``ValueError`` and no instance is
        returned. The restored key is equal by value to the original.
        """
        w, elements = _decode_v1(data, _PUBLIC_KEY_MAGIC, "public key")
        return cls(w=w, elements=elements)


def _chain_step(value: bytes) -> bytes:
    return hashlib.sha256(_DOMAIN + value).digest()


def _chain_walk(value: bytes, steps: int) -> bytes:
    for _ in range(steps):
        value = _chain_step(value)
    return value


def _message_digits(digest: bytes, w: int, b: int, l1: int) -> tuple[int, ...]:
    """Split a 256-bit digest into ``l1`` base-``B`` digits, big endian."""
    value = int.from_bytes(digest, "big")
    return tuple((value >> (256 - w * (i + 1))) & (b - 1) for i in range(l1))


def _checksum_digits(
    message_digits: Iterable[int], w: int, b: int, l2: int
) -> tuple[int, ...]:
    """``sum(B - 1 - d)`` as exactly ``l2`` base-``B`` digits, leading zeros kept."""
    checksum = sum(b - 1 - digit for digit in message_digits)
    return tuple((checksum >> (w * (l2 - 1 - i))) & (b - 1) for i in range(l2))


def _signing_digits(message: Any, w: int) -> tuple[int, ...]:
    b, l1, l2 = _params(w)
    digest = hashlib.sha256(_as_bytes(message)).digest()
    message_part = _message_digits(digest, w, b, l1)
    return message_part + _checksum_digits(message_part, w, b, l2)


class WOTSOneTimeSigner:
    """Thread-safe, single-use wrapper around a :class:`WOTSPrivateKey`.

    The first :meth:`sign` call returns the ordinary :func:`wots_sign`
    signature and marks the key as used; every later call raises
    :class:`~pqattest.KeyExhaustedError`. The guard is per instance and per
    process — copying the private key, calling the stateless :func:`wots_sign`
    directly or reusing the key in another process is the caller's
    responsibility. State can be persisted with :meth:`checkpoint` and
    restored in another process with :meth:`from_checkpoint`; the checkpoint
    contains the private key in the clear and is protected only by a SHA-256
    checksum against accidental corruption, so callers must store it securely.
    :meth:`sign_with_checkpoint` pairs the single signature with the
    post-sign checkpoint in one atomic call.
    """

    __slots__ = ("_lock", "_private_key", "_public_key", "_used")

    def __init__(self, private_key: WOTSPrivateKey) -> None:
        if not isinstance(private_key, WOTSPrivateKey):
            raise TypeError("private_key must be a WOTSPrivateKey")
        self._restore_state(private_key, self._public_key_from(private_key), False)

    @staticmethod
    def _public_key_from(private_key: WOTSPrivateKey) -> WOTSPublicKey:
        b = 1 << private_key.w
        return WOTSPublicKey(
            w=private_key.w,
            elements=tuple(
                _chain_walk(start, b - 1) for start in private_key.elements
            ),
        )

    def _restore_state(
        self,
        private_key: WOTSPrivateKey,
        public_key: WOTSPublicKey,
        used: bool,
    ) -> None:
        self._lock = threading.Lock()
        self._private_key = private_key
        self._public_key = public_key
        self._used = used

    @property
    def public_key(self) -> WOTSPublicKey:
        """Public key derived from the wrapped private key (read-only)."""
        return self._public_key

    @property
    def used(self) -> bool:
        """``True`` once a signature has been produced (read-only)."""
        return self._used

    def sign(self, message: Any) -> tuple[bytes, ...]:
        """Sign once.

        Behaves exactly like :func:`wots_sign` on the first successful call,
        accepting ``bytes``/``bytearray``/``str``; an unsupported message type
        raises the same ``TypeError`` that :func:`wots_sign` raises without
        consuming the key. Any later call raises
        :class:`~pqattest.KeyExhaustedError`. Concurrent calls are serialised
        on one lock so that at most one succeeds and every loser raises
        :class:`~pqattest.KeyExhaustedError`.
        """
        with self._lock:
            if self._used:
                raise KeyExhaustedError("this one-time signing key has already been used")
            signature = wots_sign(message, self._private_key)
            self._used = True
            return signature

    def _checkpoint_bytes(self) -> bytes:
        """Serialise the signer state; the caller holds the lock."""
        body = (
            _CHECKPOINT_MAGIC
            + bytes((_CHECKPOINT_VERSION, self._private_key.w, int(self._used)))
            + len(self._private_key.elements).to_bytes(2, "big")
            + b"".join(self._private_key.elements)
        )
        return body + hashlib.sha256(body).digest()

    def checkpoint(self) -> bytes:
        """Serialise the signer state (private key plus ``used``) to ``bytes``.

        The v1 layout is: the 8-byte magic ``b"PQAWCP\\0\\0"``; one byte each
        for the version (1), ``w`` and ``used`` (0 or 1); the element count as
        2 big-endian bytes (67 for ``w=4``, 34 for ``w=8``); every private key
        element in chain order (32 bytes each); and finally the SHA-256 of all
        preceding content. Encoding is deterministic: the same state always
        produces the same bytes.

        The checkpoint shares the signing lock, so a concurrent snapshot
        reflects the state either immediately before or immediately after an
        in-flight :meth:`sign`, never part-way through one. The blob contains
        the private key in the clear and the trailing hash only detects
        accidental corruption — store it as a secret.
        """
        with self._lock:
            return self._checkpoint_bytes()

    def sign_with_checkpoint(self, message: Any) -> tuple[tuple[bytes, ...], bytes]:
        """Sign once and snapshot the used state in one atomic step.

        Behaves like :meth:`sign` — same ``bytes``/``bytearray``/``str``
        message rules, same one-time W-OTS signature and the same
        post-sign ``used=True`` state, all under the signing lock — but
        instead of the signature alone it returns ``(signature,
        checkpoint)``: the first half is the ordinary immutable signature
        tuple that :meth:`sign` returns, value-for-value identical to
        calling :meth:`sign` on the same message from the same starting
        state, and the second is the ``bytes`` that :meth:`checkpoint`
        returns immediately after signing, byte-for-byte the same v1
        encoding holding the private key and ``used=1``. Pairing the two
        halves in one call keeps the signature and the state it advanced
        to together, so a caller can never match a signature against a
        checkpoint taken at the wrong point under concurrency.

        A rejected message type raises ``TypeError`` without consuming the
        key, and an already used instance raises
        :class:`~pqattest.KeyExhaustedError`; a failed call returns no
        partial result. The whole call — signature, ``used`` flip and
        snapshot — linearises with :meth:`sign` and :meth:`checkpoint`
        under the same lock, so at most one concurrent caller succeeds,
        and no randomness is drawn. The returned checkpoint still carries
        the private key in the clear and its trailing hash only detects
        accidental corruption — it offers no authentication, encryption or
        atomic persistence, so confidentiality, durable storage and
        rollback protection remain the caller's responsibility.
        """
        message = _as_bytes(message)
        with self._lock:
            if self._used:
                raise KeyExhaustedError("this one-time signing key has already been used")
            signature = wots_sign(message, self._private_key)
            self._used = True
            return signature, self._checkpoint_bytes()

    def sign_with_auth_state(
        self, message: Any, *, key: Any, generation: Any
    ) -> tuple[tuple[bytes, ...], bytes]:
        """Sign once and return the advanced state as a v2 auth envelope.

        Behaves like :meth:`sign` — same ``bytes``/``bytearray``/``str``
        message rules, same one-time signature and the same post-sign
        ``used=True`` state, all under the signing lock — but instead of the
        signature alone it returns ``(signature, envelope)``: the first half
        is the ordinary immutable W-OTS signature tuple that :meth:`sign`
        returns, and the second is the :func:`auth_state_wrap` v2 envelope
        (``bytes``) over the v1 :meth:`checkpoint` bytes of the used state
        with ``scheme="wots"`` and the given ``key`` and ``generation``. The
        wrapped checkpoint is byte-for-byte identical to the one
        :meth:`checkpoint` returns immediately after signing, so the envelope
        is byte-for-byte identical to signing and then wrapping an explicit
        checkpoint. Pairing the two halves in one call keeps the signature
        and the state it advanced to together, so a caller can never match a
        signature against a checkpoint taken at the wrong point under
        concurrency.

        Every argument is validated before the key is spent: ``key`` is
        keyword-only and must be a non-empty ``bytes``/``bytearray`` shared
        secret; ``generation`` is keyword-only and must be a non-boolean
        integer in ``0 .. 2**64 - 1``. A wrong message or key type raises
        ``TypeError``; an empty key or an out-of-range generation raises
        ``ValueError``; an already used instance raises
        :class:`~pqattest.KeyExhaustedError`. Every failure leaves ``used``
        untouched and returns no partial result. The whole call — signature,
        ``used`` flip, snapshot and wrapping — linearises with :meth:`sign`
        and :meth:`checkpoint` under the same lock, and no randomness is
        drawn. The envelope is plaintext and authenticated only; it provides
        neither encryption nor protection against replay or rollback on its
        own.
        """
        message = _as_bytes(message)
        key_bytes = _validate_key(key)
        generation_value = _validate_generation(generation, "generation")
        with self._lock:
            if self._used:
                raise KeyExhaustedError("this one-time signing key has already been used")
            signature = wots_sign(message, self._private_key)
            self._used = True
            checkpoint = self._checkpoint_bytes()
            envelope = auth_state_wrap(
                checkpoint,
                scheme="wots",
                key=key_bytes,
                generation=generation_value,
            )
            return signature, envelope

    @classmethod
    def from_checkpoint(cls, data: Any) -> "WOTSOneTimeSigner":
        """Restore a signer from ``checkpoint()`` output without randomness.

        ``data`` must be ``bytes`` or ``bytearray``; anything else raises
        ``TypeError``. A bad magic, version, ``w``, ``used`` flag, element
        count, length, truncation, trailing data or checksum mismatch raises
        ``ValueError`` and no instance is returned. The private key and the
        public key rebuilt from it are identical to the original's, so a
        restored unused signer still allows exactly one signature and a
        checkpoint taken after signing restores a signer whose every call
        raises :class:`~pqattest.KeyExhaustedError`.
        """
        if not isinstance(data, (bytes, bytearray)):
            raise TypeError("checkpoint data must be bytes or bytearray")
        data = bytes(data)
        header = _CHECKPOINT_HEADER_BYTES
        if len(data) < header + _CHECKPOINT_CHECKSUM_BYTES:
            raise ValueError("checkpoint is too short")
        body, checksum = data[:-_CHECKPOINT_CHECKSUM_BYTES], data[-_CHECKPOINT_CHECKSUM_BYTES:]
        if body[:8] != _CHECKPOINT_MAGIC:
            raise ValueError("bad checkpoint magic")
        if body[8] != _CHECKPOINT_VERSION:
            raise ValueError(f"unsupported checkpoint version: {body[8]}")
        w = _validate_w(body[9])
        used_byte = body[10]
        if used_byte not in (0, 1):
            raise ValueError("used flag must be 0 or 1")
        element_count = int.from_bytes(body[11:13], "big")
        _, l1, l2 = _params(w)
        chains = l1 + l2
        if element_count != chains:
            raise ValueError("element count does not match the chain count for w")
        if len(body) != header + element_count * ELEMENT_BYTES:
            raise ValueError("checkpoint length does not match the element count")
        if hashlib.sha256(body).digest() != checksum:
            raise ValueError("checkpoint checksum mismatch")
        elements = tuple(
            body[header + i * ELEMENT_BYTES : header + (i + 1) * ELEMENT_BYTES]
            for i in range(element_count)
        )
        private_key = WOTSPrivateKey(w=w, elements=elements)
        signer = cls.__new__(cls)
        signer._restore_state(
            private_key, cls._public_key_from(private_key), bool(used_byte)
        )
        return signer

    @classmethod
    def from_auth_state(
        cls, data: Any, *, key: Any, min_generation: Any = None, claim: Any
    ) -> tuple["WOTSOneTimeSigner", int]:
        """Restore a signer from a v2 ``"wots"`` envelope and claim it once.

        Combines v2 verification, the generation floor and the v1 checkpoint
        restore in one call without drawing randomness, and — only once
        everything has succeeded — performs the external monotonic claim so a
        caller can never accept a restored key without also claiming its
        generation. Only an envelope produced by :func:`auth_state_wrap` with
        ``scheme="wots"`` is accepted; no new format is introduced.
        ``key``, ``min_generation`` and ``claim`` are keyword-only. Returns
        ``(signer, generation)``: the restored :class:`WOTSOneTimeSigner`
        (equal to :meth:`from_checkpoint` on the embedded payload) and the
        non-negative uint64 generation carried in the envelope.

        ``data`` must be ``bytes`` or ``bytearray``; ``key`` must be a
        non-empty ``bytes``/``bytearray`` shared secret; ``min_generation``
        must be ``None`` or a non-boolean integer in ``0 .. 2**64 - 1``;
        ``claim`` must be callable. A wrong type (including a boolean floor or
        a non-callable claim) raises ``TypeError``. The v2 HMAC tag is
        verified first with :func:`hmac.compare_digest`; the envelope scheme
        is then fixed to ``"wots"``, the payload magic checked and the
        generation floor applied; only afterwards is the untouched payload
        handed to :meth:`from_checkpoint`. Once the checkpoint is restored,
        ``claim`` is called exactly once with the single token
        ``("wots", generation)``; the restore succeeds only when that call
        returns ``True`` (compared by identity), and any exception it raises
        propagates untouched. An empty key, a bad tag or envelope, a non-wots
        scheme (including a v1 envelope), a generation below the floor, an
        invalid checkpoint, or a claim that is not ``True`` raises
        ``ValueError`` and the callback is never invoked on such a failure.
        """
        return _restore_auth_state(
            "wots",
            data,
            key=key,
            min_generation=min_generation,
            claim=claim,
            restore=cls.from_checkpoint,
        )


def wots_keygen(
    *,
    w: int = 4,
    token_bytes: Callable[[int], bytes] = secrets.token_bytes,
) -> tuple[WOTSPrivateKey, WOTSPublicKey]:
    """Generate a fresh W-OTS key pair.

    ``w`` selects the Winternitz parameter and must be 4 or 8. Every chain
    starts at a random 32-byte value from ``token_bytes``; the public key
    stores each chain's step ``B - 1`` endpoint.
    """
    w = _validate_w(w)
    b, l1, l2 = _params(w)
    starts = tuple(bytes(token_bytes(ELEMENT_BYTES)) for _ in range(l1 + l2))
    for start in starts:
        if len(start) != ELEMENT_BYTES:
            raise ValueError(f"token_bytes must return {ELEMENT_BYTES} bytes")
    private_key = WOTSPrivateKey(w=w, elements=starts)
    endpoints = tuple(_chain_walk(start, b - 1) for start in starts)
    return private_key, WOTSPublicKey(w=w, elements=endpoints)


def wots_sign(message: Any, private_key: WOTSPrivateKey) -> tuple[bytes, ...]:
    """Sign ``message``: for each digit ``d`` reveal chain value at step ``d``.

    Message digits come first, followed by the fixed-width checksum digits.
    """
    if not isinstance(private_key, WOTSPrivateKey):
        raise TypeError("private_key must be a WOTSPrivateKey")
    digits = _signing_digits(message, private_key.w)
    return tuple(
        _chain_walk(private_key.elements[i], digit)
        for i, digit in enumerate(digits)
    )


def wots_verify(
    message: Any, signature: Sequence[Any], public_key: WOTSPublicKey
) -> bool:
    """Complete the remaining chain steps and compare every public endpoint.

    Returns ``False`` for any structural, parameter or content mismatch; only
    a wrong key *type* raises ``TypeError``.
    """
    if not isinstance(public_key, WOTSPublicKey):
        raise TypeError("public_key must be a WOTSPublicKey")
    w = public_key.w
    b, l1, l2 = _params(w)
    length = l1 + l2

    try:
        parts = tuple(bytes(part) for part in signature)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return False
    if len(parts) != length or len(public_key.elements) != length:
        return False
    if any(len(part) != ELEMENT_BYTES for part in parts):
        return False

    try:
        digits = _signing_digits(message, w)
    except TypeError:
        return False
    for i, digit in enumerate(digits):
        endpoint = _chain_walk(parts[i], b - 1 - digit)
        if endpoint != public_key.elements[i]:
            return False
    return True


def wots_signature_to_bytes(signature: Any, *, w: int) -> bytes:
    """Serialise a stateless W-OTS signature to the versioned v1 wire format.

    ``signature`` must be a ``tuple`` whose members are all ``bytes`` — the
    shape :func:`wots_sign` returns; anything else raises ``TypeError``.
    ``w`` is keyword-only and must be 4 or 8 (``ValueError`` otherwise); the
    signature must contain exactly the chain count for ``w`` (67 or 34
    elements) and every element must be exactly 32 bytes, else ``ValueError``.

    The layout is the 8-byte magic ``b"PQAWSIG\\0"``; one byte each for the
    version (1) and ``w``; the element count as 2 big-endian bytes; then every
    signature element in chain order, 32 bytes each. Encoding is
    deterministic: the same signature and ``w`` always produce the same
    bytes.
    """
    if not isinstance(signature, tuple):
        raise TypeError("signature must be a tuple of 32-byte values")
    for element in signature:
        if not isinstance(element, bytes):
            raise TypeError("every signature element must be bytes")
    w = _validate_w(w)
    chains = _chain_count(w)
    if len(signature) != chains:
        raise ValueError(f"signature must contain exactly {chains} elements for w={w}")
    for element in signature:
        if len(element) != ELEMENT_BYTES:
            raise ValueError(f"every signature element must be exactly {ELEMENT_BYTES} bytes")
    return _encode_v1(_SIGNATURE_MAGIC, w, signature)


def wots_signature_from_bytes(data: Any) -> tuple[int, tuple[bytes, ...]]:
    """Parse ``wots_signature_to_bytes()`` output back into ``(w, elements)``.

    ``data`` must be ``bytes`` or ``bytearray``; anything else raises
    ``TypeError``. A bad magic, an unknown version, an invalid ``w``, an
    element count that does not match the chain count for ``w``, truncation
    or trailing data raises ``ValueError``. The returned ``elements`` are an
    immutable ``tuple`` of 32-byte ``bytes`` in the original chain order,
    ready for :func:`wots_verify`.
    """
    return _decode_v1(data, _SIGNATURE_MAGIC, "signature")


def _wots_signature_matches_key(signature: Any, public_key: Any) -> bool:
    """Non-raising parameter/count check for a W-OTS proof pair."""
    if not isinstance(public_key, WOTSPublicKey):
        return False
    try:
        w = _validate_w(public_key.w)
    except (ValueError, AttributeError):
        return False
    if not isinstance(signature, tuple) or len(signature) != _chain_count(w):
        return False
    return all(
        isinstance(element, bytes) and len(element) == ELEMENT_BYTES
        for element in signature
    )


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class WOTSProof:
    """Frozen, self-contained bundle of one W-OTS public key and one signature.

    Unlike a bare signature tuple (whose wire encoding needs ``w`` supplied
    separately), a proof carries the :class:`WOTSPublicKey` that constrains
    its signature, so it can be transported on its own as a single byte block
    and verified with :meth:`verify`. The proof stores no message and is a
    pure serialisation container: it offers neither authentication nor
    encryption of the wrapper itself, draws no randomness, generates
    no keys and keeps no state.
    """

    public_key: WOTSPublicKey
    signature: tuple[bytes, ...]

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if not isinstance(self.public_key, WOTSPublicKey):
            raise TypeError("public_key must be a WOTSPublicKey")
        if not isinstance(self.signature, tuple):
            raise TypeError("signature must be a tuple of 32-byte values")
        if not all(isinstance(element, bytes) for element in self.signature):
            raise TypeError("every signature element must be bytes")
        if not _wots_signature_matches_key(self.signature, self.public_key):
            raise ValueError(
                "signature chain count or elements do not match the public key"
            )

    def to_bytes(self) -> bytes:
        """Serialise to the versioned v1 proof wire format as ``bytes``.

        The layout is the 8-byte magic ``b"PQAWPRF\\0"``; one version byte
        (1); the public-key and signature lengths as 4 big-endian bytes each;
        then the existing v1 encodings of the public key and of the signature
        constrained by that key, in that order (the inner encodings are
        reused unchanged). Encoding is deterministic: the same proof always
        produces the same bytes. A field corrupted by bypassing the frozen
        constructor raises ``ValueError`` instead of producing malformed
        bytes.
        """
        if not isinstance(self, WOTSProof):
            raise TypeError("to_bytes must be called on a WOTSProof")
        try:
            key_bytes = self.public_key.to_bytes()
            signature_bytes = wots_signature_to_bytes(
                self.signature, w=self.public_key.w
            )
        except (TypeError, AttributeError) as exc:
            raise ValueError(f"corrupted proof field: {exc}") from exc
        return (
            _PROOF_MAGIC
            + bytes((_PROOF_VERSION,))
            + len(key_bytes).to_bytes(4, "big")
            + len(signature_bytes).to_bytes(4, "big")
            + key_bytes
            + signature_bytes
        )

    @classmethod
    def from_bytes(cls, data: Any) -> "WOTSProof":
        """Parse ``to_bytes()`` output back into a :class:`WOTSProof`.

        ``data`` must be ``bytes`` or ``bytearray``; anything else raises
        ``TypeError``. The embedded public key is recovered first and then
        constrains the signature. A bad magic, an unknown version, a length
        field that is out of bounds or disagrees with the actual content,
        truncation, trailing data, an invalid nested encoding, or a signature
        inconsistent with the key (wrong ``w`` or chain count) raises
        ``ValueError`` and no half-valid object is returned.
        """
        if not isinstance(data, (bytes, bytearray)):
            raise TypeError("proof data must be bytes or bytearray")
        data = bytes(data)
        if len(data) < _PROOF_HEADER_BYTES:
            raise ValueError("proof encoding is truncated")
        if data[:8] != _PROOF_MAGIC:
            raise ValueError("bad proof magic")
        if data[8] != _PROOF_VERSION:
            raise ValueError(f"unsupported proof version: {data[8]}")
        key_length = int.from_bytes(data[9:13], "big")
        signature_length = int.from_bytes(data[13:17], "big")
        key_end = _PROOF_HEADER_BYTES + key_length
        signature_end = key_end + signature_length
        if key_length == 0 or signature_length == 0:
            raise ValueError("a length field must not be zero")
        if key_end > len(data) or signature_end > len(data):
            raise ValueError("proof encoding is truncated")
        if signature_end < len(data):
            raise ValueError("trailing data after the proof encoding")
        public_key = WOTSPublicKey.from_bytes(data[_PROOF_HEADER_BYTES:key_end])
        w, signature = wots_signature_from_bytes(data[key_end:signature_end])
        if w != public_key.w:
            raise ValueError("signature w does not match the public key")
        return cls(public_key=public_key, signature=signature)

    def verify(self, message: Any) -> bool:
        """Verify the embedded signature against the embedded public key.

        Accepts ``bytes``/``bytearray``/``str`` exactly like
        :func:`wots_verify`, to which this call delegates; it returns
        ``True`` only for the message that was actually signed. Any change to
        the message, public key or signature, an illegal message type, or
        fields corrupted by bypassing the frozen constructor returns
        ``False`` instead of raising. The proof itself carries no message and
        cannot authenticate its own origin.
        """
        try:
            return wots_verify(message, self.signature, self.public_key)
        except Exception:
            return False

726	class LamportProof:
727	    """Frozen, self-contained bundle of one Lamport public key and one signature.
728	
729	    Unlike a bare signature tuple (whose wire encoding needs the
730	    corresponding :class:`PublicKey` plus ``bits`` supplied separately), a
731	    proof carries the :class:`PublicKey` that constrains its signature, so it
732	    can be transported on its own as a single byte block and verified with
733	    :meth:`verify`. The proof stores no message and is a pure serialisation
734	    container: it offers neither authentication nor encryption of the wrapper
735	    itself, draws no randomness, generates no keys and keeps no state.
736	    """
737	
738	    public_key: PublicKey
739	    signature: tuple[bytes, ...]
740	
741	    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
742	        if not isinstance(self.public_key, PublicKey):
743	            raise TypeError("public_key must be a PublicKey")
744	        if not isinstance(self.signature, tuple):
745	            raise TypeError("signature must be a tuple of 32-byte values")
746	        if not all(isinstance(element, bytes) for element in self.signature):
747	            raise TypeError("every signature element must be bytes")
748	        if not _lamport_signature_matches_key(self.signature, self.public_key):
749	            raise ValueError("signature bits or element count do not match the public key")
750	
751	    def to_bytes(self) -> bytes:
752	        """Serialise to the versioned v1 proof wire format as ``bytes``.
753	
754	        The layout is the 8-byte magic ``b"PQALPRF\\0"``; one version byte
755	        (1); the public-key and signature lengths as 4 big-endian bytes each;
756	        then the existing v1 encodings of the public key and of the signature
757	        constrained by that key, in that order (the inner encodings are
758	        reused unchanged). Encoding is deterministic: the same proof always
759	        produces the same bytes. A field corrupted by bypassing the frozen
760	        constructor raises ``ValueError`` instead of producing malformed
761	        bytes.
762	        """
763	        if not isinstance(self, LamportProof):
764	            raise TypeError("to_bytes must be called on a LamportProof")
765	        try:
766	            key_bytes = self.public_key.to_bytes()
767	            signature_bytes = lamport_signature_to_bytes(
768	                self.signature, bits=self.public_key.bits
769	            )
770	        except (TypeError, AttributeError) as exc:
771	            raise ValueError(f"corrupted proof field: {exc}") from exc
772	        return (
773	            _PROOF_MAGIC
774	            + bytes((_PROOF_VERSION,))
775	            + len(key_bytes).to_bytes(4, "big")
776	            + len(signature_bytes).to_bytes(4, "big")
777	            + key_bytes
778	            + signature_bytes
779	        )

781	    @classmethod
782	    def from_bytes(cls, data: Any) -> "LamportProof":
783	        """Parse ``to_bytes()`` output back into a :class:`LamportProof`.
784	
785	        ``data`` must be ``bytes`` or ``bytearray``; anything else raises
786	        ``TypeError``. The embedded public key is recovered first and then
787	        constrains the signature. A bad magic, an unknown version, a length
788	        field that is out of bounds or disagrees with the actual content,
789	        truncation, trailing data, an invalid nested encoding, or a signature
790	        inconsistent with the key (wrong bits or count) raises ``ValueError``
791	        and no half-valid object is returned.
792	        """
793	        if not isinstance(data, (bytes, bytearray)):
794	            raise TypeError("proof data must be bytes or bytearray")
795	        data = bytes(data)
796	        if len(data) < _PROOF_HEADER_BYTES:
797	            raise ValueError("proof encoding is truncated")
798	        if data[:8] != _PROOF_MAGIC:
799	            raise ValueError("bad proof magic")
800	        if data[8] != _PROOF_VERSION:
801	            raise ValueError(f"unsupported proof version: {data[8]}")
802	        key_length = int.from_bytes(data[9:13], "big")
803	        signature_length = int.from_bytes(data[13:17], "big")
804	        key_end = _PROOF_HEADER_BYTES + key_length
805	        signature_end = key_end + signature_length
806	        if key_length == 0 or signature_length == 0:
807	            raise ValueError("a length field must not be zero")
808	        if key_end > len(data) or signature_end > len(data):
809	            raise ValueError("proof encoding is truncated")
810	        if signature_end < len(data):
811	            raise ValueError("trailing data after the proof encoding")
812	        public_key = PublicKey.from_bytes(data[_PROOF_HEADER_BYTES:key_end])
813	        bits, signature = lamport_signature_from_bytes(data[key_end:signature_end])
814	        if bits != public_key.bits:
815	            raise ValueError("signature bits do not match the public key")
816	        return cls(public_key=public_key, signature=signature)
817	
818	    def verify(self, message: Any) -> bool:
819	        """Verify the embedded signature against the embedded public key.
820	
821	        Accepts ``bytes``/``bytearray``/``str`` exactly like :func:`verify`,
822	        to which this call delegates; it returns ``True`` only for the
823	        message that was actually signed. Any change to the message, public
824	        key or signature, an illegal message type, or fields corrupted by
825	        bypassing the frozen constructor returns ``False`` instead of
826	        raising. The proof itself carries no message and cannot authenticate
827	        its own origin.
828	        """
829	        try:
830	            return verify(message, self.signature, self.public_key)
831	        except Exception:
832	            return False

847	    encryption of the wrapper itself, draws no randomness, generates no

102:- `LamportProof(public_key, signature)` — 冻结的证明值对象，字段须分别为 `PublicKey` 与成员全为 `bytes` 的签名元组（字段类型错误抛 `TypeError`，签名比特数/元素计数与公钥不一致抛 `ValueError`）；把一把 Lamport 公钥和一份签名打包成一份可**独立传输**的证明。证明包不存消息，本身不提供认证或加密，不取随机数、不生成密钥、不保存状态
103:- `LamportProof.to_bytes()` / `LamportProof.from_bytes(data)` — 证明包的版本化二进制编解码；编码确定、同值同字节。`from_bytes` 只接受 `bytes`/`bytearray`（其他类型抛 `TypeError`），解析时先恢复包内公钥、再以它约束签名；坏魔数、未知版本、长度字段不符、截断、尾随数据、嵌套编码非法或公钥与签名交叉不一致均抛 `ValueError`，不返回半有效对象；字段被绕过冻结构造破坏时编码抛 `ValueError`，不产出畸形字节
104:- `LamportProof.verify(message)` — 接受 `bytes`/`bytearray`/`str`，等价于 `verify(message, proof.signature, proof.public_key)`；只对被签署的消息返回 `True`。篡改保证只覆盖可达成的部分：消息、消息位选中的公钥分支或签名元素被改动后返回 `False`（非法消息类型同样返回 `False`，不抛异常）；**未被消息位选中的 Lamport 公钥分支不在保证之内**，须由调用方在公钥完整性层兜底

- `OtsPairProof.verify(message)` — 接受 `bytes`/`bytearray`/`str`，对同一消息依次校验包内两份证明，全部通过才返回 `True`；非法消息类型、任一侧失败、字段畸形或绕过冻结构造破坏的对象均返回 `False`，不抛异常。篡改保证只覆盖可达成的部分：消息、消息位用到的公钥分支与签名元素被改动时返回 `False`；**未被消息位选中的 Lamport 公钥分支不在其内**，由调用方在公钥完整性层兜底

from pqattest import (
    keygen, sign, LamportProof, PublicKey,
    wots_keygen, wots_sign, WOTSProof, WOTSPublicKey,
)

# Lamport
priv, pub = keygen()
sig = sign(b"position claim", priv)
proof = LamportProof(public_key=pub, signature=sig)

assert proof.verify_bound(b"position claim", public_key=pub) is True
assert proof.verify_bound("position claim", public_key=pub) is True
assert proof.verify_bound(bytearray(b"position claim"), public_key=pub) is True
# equal-by-value, different instance
assert proof.verify_bound(b"position claim", public_key=PublicKey(pub.digests)) is True
# wrong message / unsupported message type
assert proof.verify_bound(b"other", public_key=pub) is False
assert proof.verify_bound(None, public_key=pub) is False
assert proof.verify_bound(123, public_key=pub) is False
# wrong expected key value
_, other_pub = keygen()
assert proof.verify_bound(b"position claim", public_key=other_pub) is False
# wrong expected key type -> TypeError
for bad in ("not-a-key", None, 42, WOTSPublicKey(w=4, elements=(b"\x00"*32,)*67)):
    try:
        proof.verify_bound(b"position claim", public_key=bad)
        raise AssertionError("expected TypeError")
    except TypeError:
        pass
# keyword-only
try:
    proof.verify_bound(b"position claim", pub)
    raise AssertionError("expected TypeError")
except TypeError:
    pass
# unselected Lamport branch swapped in embedded key -> bound check blocks it
digests = list(pub.digests)
bits = pub.bits
# find a branch not selected by the message bits
from pqattest import message_bits
mb = message_bits(b"position claim", bits=bits)
i = 0
digests[2*i + (1-mb[i])] = b"\xff"*32
rogue = LamportProof(public_key=PublicKey(tuple(digests)), signature=sig)
assert rogue.verify(b"position claim") is True          # plain verify gap
assert rogue.verify_bound(b"position claim", public_key=pub) is False
# corrupted fields via bypassed frozen constructor
rogue2 = LamportProof.__new__(LamportProof)
object.__setattr__(rogue2, "public_key", "garbage")
object.__setattr__(rogue2, "signature", sig)
assert rogue2.verify_bound(b"position claim", public_key=pub) is False
rogue3 = LamportProof.__new__(LamportProof)
object.__setattr__(rogue3, "signature", sig)
assert rogue3.verify_bound(b"position claim", public_key=pub) is False
# determinism / repeatability
assert proof.verify_bound(b"position claim", public_key=pub) is True

# WOTS
wpriv, wpub = wots_keygen()
wsig = wots_sign(b"position claim", wpriv)
wproof = WOTSProof(public_key=wpub, signature=wsig)
assert wproof.verify_bound(b"position claim", public_key=wpub) is True
assert wproof.verify_bound(b"position claim", public_key=WOTSPublicKey(w=wpub.w, elements=wpub.elements)) is True
assert wproof.verify_bound(b"other", public_key=wpub) is False
assert wproof.verify_bound(None, public_key=wpub) is False
_, wother = wots_keygen()
assert wproof.verify_bound(b"position claim", public_key=wother) is False
try:
    wproof.verify_bound(b"position claim", public_key=pub)  # Lamport PublicKey
    raise AssertionError("expected TypeError")
except TypeError:
    pass
try:
    wproof.verify_bound(b"position claim", wpub)
    raise AssertionError("expected TypeError")
except TypeError:
    pass
wrogue = WOTSProof.__new__(WOTSProof)
object.__setattr__(wrogue, "public_key", None)
object.__setattr__(wrogue, "signature", wsig)
assert wrogue.verify_bound(b"position claim", public_key=wpub) is False
assert wproof.verify_bound(b"position claim", public_key=wpub) is True

print("all smoke checks passed")
EOF
